reference_answer: PREST is the OOI seafloor-pressure instrument family. The corpus identifies PREST as the source of the SFLPRES seafloor-pressure product and the COSZO pressure workflow as handling absolute seafloor-pressure acquisition, conversion, gap detection, and timing diagnostics for RCA stations.
COVIS is the Cabled Array Vent Imaging Sonar. It provides acoustic imaging and in-situ observations used to study deep-seafloor hydrothermal discharge at the RCA ASHES hydrothermal field.

required_citations.title: Acoustic and In-Situ Observations of Deep Seafloor Hydrothermal Discharge An OOI Cabled Array ASHES

reference_answer: CTDPFA110 is the MARUM CTD-DO instrument. The corpus identifies its PI-operated data location and the OOI instrument page; an answer should identify it as CTD and dissolved-oxygen instrumentation and cite the data route.

reference_answer: The HYS14 StationXML record contains four channel epochs: LDO, LK1, UDO, and UK1. The station is OO.HYS14; answers should retain the StationXML provenance and distinguish channel metadata from the Chronfix MHZ stream record.

COVIS raw and processed holdings are routed through the audited PI Portal COVIS dataset endpoint. The corpus-first answer should provide the PI Portal location; a live browse or download occurs only after the user asks for current files or selected files.

reference_answer: MARUM CTD-DO data for CTDPFA110 are available from the audited PI Portal endpoint. A corpus answer should provide that route and the OOI instrument citation; live file discovery is optional only when the user requests current holdings.

reference_answer: The Regional Cabled Array is the OOI cabled observatory serving the northeast Pacific and Juan de Fuca Plate. It connects seafloor infrastructure, instruments, power, and communications for sustained observations.

An OOI reference designator is the stable identifier used to identify OOI assets and their delivery methods or streams. It is the identifier an answer should use when directing a user to OOI M2M vocabulary, stream discovery, or a data-request plan.

Science junction boxes are cabled-infrastructure interfaces that distribute power and communications and provide instrument connections at RCA sites. Answers should cite the junction-box infrastructure source rather than describe them as sensors.

At least two corpus-grounded starting points are the work titled 'Seismic imaging of the internal workings of Axial Seamount on the Juan de Fuca Ridge' and 'Structure, Seismicity, and Accretionary Processes at the Hot Spot-Influenced Axial Seamount on the Juan de Fuca Ridge.' A response must cite the returned works rather than claim an exhaustive bibliography.

required_citations.title: Seismic imaging of the internal workings of Axial Seamount on the Juan de Fuca Ridge

reference_answer: No. Existing public QA/QC plots are evidence to inspect, not proof by themselves that an instrument passed QA/QC. The answer should distinguish a plot from validated QA/QC status and use the QAQC routing policy for current or human-in-the-loop evidence.
This is a live-current request. The agent must select `qaqc_search_plots` and use the corpus routing policy; it must not claim that cached corpus material is a current plot.

This is an execution request. The agent must select `qaqc_generate_plots`, disclose that execution is controlled by the QAQC pipeline switch, and avoid claiming a plot was generated unless the tool result confirms it.
A HYS14 clock-correction answer must use the HYS14 Chronfix routing policy and disclose the currently applicable correction and provenance. It must not hard-code a correction value from a snapshot.

The corpus policy says that the HYS14 OBS clock correction derived and validated from MHZ applies to channels on that same OBS instrument when technically justified; it must exclude PREST, VEL3D, and other instruments. A response must state the correction provenance and scope.
The latest correction-file request requires the live Chronfix model lookup. The result must report the resolved correction bundle, file fingerprint, and provenance.

Timestamp correction requires the live correction model and must return the applied model hash or file fingerprint with the converted true UTC value. It must not use a static correction embedded in a test answer.
This is a current UTC-day question. The agent must call `axial_count_events` with `day` set to `yesterday` and report the live-versus-snapshot source returned by the tool.
This is a date-specific live event request. The agent must call `axial_search_events` with the requested UTC date and return the bounded event records plus source provenance.
The Axial catalog is a near-real-time earthquake catalog; fixed corpus material can explain its coverage and counting semantics, but exact current counts require the daily-count tool.
A magnitude histogram is a requested derived visualization. The agent must select `axial_plot_events` or the current Axial figure tool and must not fabricate a histogram from monthly-summary chunks.

A map of yesterday's earthquakes is a current visual request. The agent must use `axial_get_figure` or `axial_plot_events`, identify the UTC date and source, and return the resulting figure provenance.
Current RCA instrument status requires `nereus_instrument_status`. The answer must state its observation timestamp and must not present a packaged Nereus snapshot as current status.
The PN1B figure record is the 'PN1B proposed-node map.' A valid response must cite that stable figure ID and avoid substituting the PN1C map.
A current Axial caldera map requires live figure retrieval. The response must select `axial_get_figure` and preserve the returned date, source, and figure provenance.

The corpus contains both a PN1C proposed-node map and a PN1C COSZO area map. A comparison must name both stable figure records and identify each annotation or provenance difference; it must not merge them into one figure.

A waveform download is an action request. The agent must first use `earthscope_plan_waveform` to validate the exact station and bounded time window, then use `earthscope_download_waveform` only when the user confirms retrieval.
Searching current COVIS PI Portal files requires `pi_portal_find_files`; it is discovery only and must not download files. Returned paths and source URLs are the expected evidence.

Discovering newly generated COSZO outputs requires a rescan through `coszo_output_status` or `coszo_list_outputs`. The answer must identify the scan time and must not infer new files from the static corpus.
A hydrophone definition is stable corpus knowledge. The answer should use the instrument-class source and must not invoke a live tool.

A correct graph answer must trace an instrument through `LOCATED_AT` to its physical site and through `DOWNLOADABLE_FROM` to its data endpoint. It must keep physical location and download location distinct.
A station-to-epoch answer must connect the station to its channel-epoch records and preserve the StationXML source provenance. It must not infer channel epochs from unrelated datasheet glossary text.
A QA/QC graph answer must connect a capability to its service and exposed tool using the `IMPLEMENTS` and `EXPOSES` relationships. It must separate a capability description from live execution.
This is a request-planning question. The agent must use `ooi_m2m_plan_request`, validate the reference designator and requested bounds, and not submit a live OOI request during planning.

Full-text acquisition is permitted only after the abstract is relevant but insufficient. The agent must use `literature_full_text_evidence` with exactly one valid work selector and return bounded cited passages rather than an uncited reconstruction.
Human-in-the-loop QA/QC notes are current operational evidence. The agent must use `qaqc_question_context` for the selected instrument or site and preserve source timestamps and tool provenance.

Current Nereus alerts and notes for a node require `nereus_node_status` or `nereus_operational_notes`; an answer must distinguish a node from an instrument and preserve the live observation timestamp.
A packaged Nereus snapshot may be summarized only as dated snapshot evidence. It must name the snapshot observation time and must not be described as current status.
File status is a current instrument-status field. The agent must use `nereus_instrument_status` and report the file-status observation returned by that tool rather than claim a static result.
Ping status is a current instrument-status field. The agent must use `nereus_instrument_status` and report the ping-status observation returned by that tool rather than claim a static result.
HYS14 is the Southern Hydrate Ridge Summit RCA seismic station. Its answer must cite StationXML and identify only the channel epochs and sensor metadata that the station record supports.
The answer must enumerate only instruments explicitly represented as seafloor-pressure instruments in the corpus, identify PREST/SFLPRES where supported, and cite each instrument record.
A valid PREST location answer must give the instrument deployment, physical site, and infrastructure node as separate graph facts, with `LOCATED_AT` provenance.
CTDPFA110 location must be stated from the MARUM CTD-DO instrument record, with the PI Portal endpoint kept separate from its physical site.
A Hydrate Ridge answer must list only instruments explicitly linked to Hydrate Ridge and cite their corresponding corpus records.
RCA graph answers must distinguish sites, infrastructure nodes, and instruments, using location and ownership/connection edges rather than treating the three as interchangeable.

PREST availability must be answered corpus-first with its documented data route. A live browse, download, or processing action is optional only when the user requests current holdings or data retrieval.
EarthScope-accessible RCA waveform answers must cite the StationXML or EarthScope/FDSN evidence for the named station and use a tool only when the user asks to retrieve a waveform.
COSZO is a project that uses RCA and related observations for coastal and ocean-system science; answers must state the corpus-supported relationship and cite both COSZO and RCA sources.

A data product is a processed or defined scientific output; a channel is a specific measured signal or metadata stream. The answer must preserve that distinction and cite the underlying product and StationXML evidence.
Literature discovery must return the cited Axial hydrothermal-vent works supported by the literature corpus and distinguish hydrothermal observations from unrelated Axial seismicity papers.
The answer must provide an exact DOI and bibliographic citation from a resolved COSZO-related pressure work; no DOI may be inferred from title text alone.
An author list must be derived from structured literature author records and associated cabled-observation works, not from unnormalized citation strings.
The QA/QC answer must describe the documented QA/QC lifecycle and available plot, HITL, routing, and controlled-generation capabilities without claiming a current instrument result.
No. The HYS14 OBS clock correction must not be applied to PREST pressure data; the routing policy explicitly separates PREST from the affected OBS channels.
A site-map answer must return a figure explicitly identified as an RCA site map and preserve its page/document provenance. Broad COSZO document chunks are insufficient without the figure record.
A datasheet-diagram answer must return a component diagram from the Datasheets collection and cite the source page; an instrument text record alone is insufficient.

Arcada is static corpus evidence in this deployment. A named instrument record should be retrieved from the Arcada collection; a live tool must not be claimed because no `arcada_retrieval` tool is registered.

A publication graph answer must traverse the work to structured authors, mentioned topics, and its source/listing collection, and must cite the specific work rather than invent coauthor or topic edges.

A figure-provenance answer must connect the figure to its page and document records and preserve the source locator. If current pixels are needed, use the figure tool only after the user requests retrieval.
